policy: Two-sided field on every strategy entry: what evidence would move the desk toward belief, and what evidence would end the hypothesis. Pre-registered rules about evidence, not predictions.

rows.name: Model side vs no-knowledge baseline
rows.rule: Every originated game. Signal = per-game contest: is our side closer to the actual margin than a constant home-margin baseline fitted on the same training weeks?
rows.evidence: contest win rate vs baseline: 0.6381 on n=105 graded games, exact binomial p=0.006, BH q<=0.10 pass=yes
rows.would_upgrade: on a later, untouched walk-forward window of >= 100 graded games the contest win rate stays above the C1 coin-flip control line (0.577) with a Wilson 95% CI lower bound above it and Benjamini-Hochberg q <= 0.10
rows.would_abandon: two consecutive walk-forward windows land at or below the C1 control line (0.577) with the CI upper bound at or below it, or the edge's sign flips on the trailing-50 window - the demotion gate returns it to paper

rows.name: Model total vs league-average baseline
rows.rule: Every originated game. Signal = per-game contest against a constant total fitted on the same training weeks.
rows.evidence: contest win rate vs baseline: 0.4476 on n=105 graded games, exact binomial p=0.3291, BH q<=0.10 pass=no
rows.would_upgrade: on a later, untouched walk-forward window of >= 100 graded games the contest win rate stays above the C1 coin-flip control line (0.577) with a Wilson 95% CI lower bound above it and Benjamini-Hochberg q <= 0.10
rows.would_abandon: two consecutive walk-forward windows land at or below the C1 control line (0.577) with the CI upper bound at or below it, or the edge's sign flips on the trailing-50 window - the demotion gate returns it to paper

rows.name: Model moneyline probability (Brier skill)

rows.evidence: Brier skill score (1 = perfect, 0 = baseline): 0.0808 on n=105 graded games, BH q<=0.10 pass=not tested (no p-value computable for this metric)
rows.would_upgrade: on a later, untouched walk-forward window of >= 100 graded games the contest win rate stays above the C1 coin-flip control line (0.577) with a Wilson 95% CI lower bound above it and Benjamini-Hochberg q <= 0.10
rows.would_abandon: two consecutive walk-forward windows land at or below the C1 control line (0.577) with the CI upper bound at or below it, or the edge's sign flips on the trailing-50 window - the demotion gate returns it to paper

rows.name: Measured home-field arbitrage vs an assumed 3.0 pts
rows.rule: Compare our fitted home-field constant to the conventional 3.0-point assumption and fire only when the gap moves the side across a whole point.
rows.evidence: fitted home-field constant (points): blank on n=105 graded games, BH q<=0.10 pass=not tested (no p-value computable for this metric)
rows.would_upgrade: the measured home-field constant stabilises across >= 3 refit windows (bootstrap CI width < 1.0 point) and departs from the assumed 3.0 points with the CI excluding it
rows.would_abandon: the fitted constant's CI covers the assumed 3.0 points for three consecutive refit windows - then no arbitrage exists and the entry is withdrawn

rows.name: Same-game double (side leg x total leg)
rows.rule: Two legs in one game. Signal = the MEASURED joint of the two leg outcomes against the product of their marginals. Payoff columns stay empty until prices exist.
rows.evidence: joint(obs) / joint(independent): 1.067 on n=105 graded games, exact binomial p=0.4167, BH q<=0.10 pass=no
rows.would_upgrade: the joint-evidence gate clears: a directly validated joint probability (measured on official results, with a CI that excludes the independence value) AND the operator's void/push rules on record, plus a per-leg price history with provenance - then the pre-registered rule is graded on fresh walk-forward decisions
rows.would_abandon: the gate stays closed: either the joint validation or the operator rules remain missing through the season window the registration froze - the combo is then retired rather than ranked on multiplied marginals
